name: eutl-installation-net-short

source.publisher: European Commission, Directorate-General for Climate Action (DG CLIMA) - Union Registry Public Website, EUTL public extracts
source.vintage_last_modified: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 10:08:26 GMT (SNAPSHOT_DATE 2026-10-22; the extract refreshes daily)
source.requests_note: one anonymous GET of the daily operators_yearly_activity extract (5,965,780 B / 1.0 s, sha256 1c7db552...) plus the EEA aggregate zip (10,794,107 B / 9.3 s, sha256 9005e05f...) used only for the in-build publisher cross-check; both stable tokenless URLs, no key
source.fetch_provenance: worker job eutl-001 (server 171845011, cx23/hel1) fetched the publisher directly; the bytes never passed through the coordinator. The panel fetch was first measured at discovery on the coordinator (5,959,551 B compressed, 2026-10-20 snapshot) and re-measured on the worker (5,965,780 B, 2026-10-22 snapshot - the daily extract grows as live-year rows arrive)

grain: one row per (REGISTRY_CODE, INSTALLATION_IDENTIFIER, PERIOD_YEAR) on the operators_yearly_activity extract, in-frame (label computable: both VERIFIED_EMISSIONS(t) and ALLOCATION(t) numeric) and with a numeric t-1 year

label.definition: net_short = 1 iff VERIFIED_EMISSIONS(t) > ALLOCATION(t); exact ties are 0 and counted

eligibility.insufficient_history_note: all of 2005 (no t-1 exists) plus each installation's first active year
eligibility.live_year_note: 2026 rows: allocation already published, verified emissions due 31 March 2027 - scorable the day the next annual compliance data lands
eligibility.dropped_feature: SURR_ALL(t-1) was probed as a surrender-history feature and dropped: missing on 10,647 of 188,205 eligible rows (measured), and a partially-defined column cannot ship

reference_baselines.note: stdlib rank AUC measured at construction on the written rows; rate tables estimated on train rows only. The label is persistent (P(short|short) = 0.8571, P(short|long) = 0.1759) but persistence does not win by construction: the announced-allocation margin_t alone beats the persistence margin.

baseline_full_model.runner: the benchmark's own train.py + validate.sh, unmodified (bundled sha256 equal the benchmark's declared hashes)
baseline_full_model.note: 0.9199 vs persistence 0.8671 on identical eval rows; no holdout AUC is quoted (the holdout never enters a workdir)

known_event_fixtures.at_installation_1_2030: advance allocation 30,485 with no verified emissions (verified in-panel)

publisher_crosscheck.method: sum the shipped panel by registry/year/activity over exactly EEA activity codes {10, 20-99} (the EEA sheet carries per-activity detail AND aggregate rows) and compare against the EEA's own EU ETS summary product

timing.prediction_instant: 30 April of compliance year t - the surrender deadline closing year t-1's compliance cycle
timing.publication_lag_observations: verified emissions for year t-1 are reported by 31 March of year t and settled at the instant; surrendered allowances are due by 30 April; year-t free allocation is fixed in advance by the phase-4 national implementation measures (the extract carries allocation rows through 2030, measured)
timing.no_early_target_knowledge: year-t verified emissions are reported by 31 March t+1 and are absent from the registry at the instant (measured: no numeric verified emissions for years after 2025 in the daily extract)
timing.vintage_caveat: features are current-snapshot values: the registry can correct entries after the fact and only the current daily extract is available, so the timing claim is stated as current-vintage with the cutoff a documented assumption

phase_drift_note: the net-short base rate rises with the ETS phase (45.53% train -> 74.02% eval -> 72.20% holdout) because the free-allocation share fell while the cap declined; reported per split and per year, not smoothed
